final_candidates.decision_summary: Conserved acidic residue in the DFIITQLFFE catalytic core; alanine removes side-chain function likely abolishing activity while retaining basic fold.

stop_reason.detail: Reasoning converged and no evidence tools are available to refine further.

history.rationale: Gly255 in the PGIFPIQGYHS motif; conserved glycines in TIM-barrel loops permit backbone flexibility, and Ala substitution can rigidify and impair catalysis. Verified G at position 255.
Buried glycine-to-alanine can perturb packing but is often tolerated; the more disruptive G257R is a stronger LOF bet. Kept as backup.
Arg157 near the active-site loop likely forms electrostatic contacts with substrate/cofactor; neutralization should reduce catalytic efficiency. Verified R at position 157.
Conserved arginine may bind substrate/FAD phosphate, so removal is plausibly deleterious, but positional role is uncertain without structure. Retained at slightly lowered confidence.
His201 may participate in proton transfer/redox chemistry typical of flavoenzyme active sites; mutation to Ala removes this function. Verified H at position 201.
Histidine can be catalytic, but position 201 role is unverified and MTHFR chemistry is FAD/NADPH-based rather than classic acid-base His catalysis. Demoted.
The DFIITQLFFE region lies in the catalytic TIM-barrel core; disrupting a conserved acidic residue here is likely to abolish activity. Alanine removes side-chain function while preserving fold.
